### Summary The audio decode-duration guard (`max_duration_s`, env `VLLM_MAX_AUDIO_DECODE_DURATION_S`, default 600s) that protects against audio decompression-bomb DoS is wired into **only** the speech-to-text path (`/v1/audio/transcriptions`). The **chat** audio path (`/v1/chat/completions`, `input_audio` content parts) calls the same decoder with **no** limit, so an **unauthenticated** client can submit a few-KB compressed audio file that expands to multiple GB of float32 PCM at decode time, OOM-killing the worker. This is a distinct sibling of **CVE-2026-5497** (video frame-count bomb, `VideoMediaIO.load_base64`) and **GHSA-pq5c-rjhq-qp7p** (image) in the same media subsystem.  Verified against `main` at HEAD `d78650c` (2026-06-16); applicable to the latest release v0.23.0.  ### Details The guard rejects long audio *during* decode (before allocation), implemented in `vllm/multimodal/media/audio.py`: - `load_audio_pyav` — metadata reject (~82-98) and live sample-count reject (~129-136) - `load_audio_soundfile` — frames reject (~165-174)  All are gated on `if max_duration_s is not None`.  It is passed in exactly **one** place — the transcription serving layer: ```python # .../speech_to_text/base/serving.py:~170-174 load_audio(buf, sr=..., max_duration_s=self.max_audio_decode_duration_s) #   self.max_audio_decode_duration_s = envs.VLLM_MAX_AUDIO_DECODE_DURATION_S  (default 600) ```  The chat path never threads it: ```python # vllm/multimodal/media/audio.py:237-238 def load_bytes(self, data: bytes) -> tuple[npt.NDArray, float]:     return load_audio(BytesIO(data), sr=None)   # no max_duration_s -> every guard above is skipped ```  Unauthenticated reachability chain (chat): `parse_input_audio` (`chat_utils.py`) -> `parse_audio` -> `connector.fetch_audio` -> `AudioMediaIO._load_data_url` -> `load_base64` -> `load_bytes` -> `load_audio(..., sr=None)`. The connector never passes `max_duration_s`, and inline `data:` URLs need no HTTP fetch (so `VLLM_AUDIO_FETCH_TIMEOUT` does not bound them). The OpenAI-compatible server has no auth by default (auth only when `--api-key` / `VLLM_API_KEY` is set).  ### Impact Unauthenticated remote denial of service (availability) via memory amplification on a default-no-auth endpoint, on any deployment serving an audio-capable model. Same class and impact as the sibling CVE-2026-5497 (video). CWE-770 / CWE-409.  ### Fix A fix was introduced in this MR: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/45908

## Summary  Current vLLM `main` lets an inference request choose the PyNvVideoCodec GPU video decoder through `media_io_kwargs.video.video_backend`, but engine GPU memory reservation is computed only from static startup configuration and `VLLM_VIDEO_LOADER_BACKEND`. If the server starts with the default OpenCV/software backend and no `--mm-ipc-gpu-memory-gb` budget, a client can still route a video request into the PyNvVideoCodec path after startup, causing frontend CUDA-context, decoder-surface, and decoded-frame GPU allocations that were not carved out of the engine KV-cache budget.  ## Technical Details  The vulnerable boundary is the split between request-time media decoding choices in the API server and startup-time memory budgeting in the engine worker. Request bodies for Chat Completions and Responses expose `media_io_kwargs`, and those values are forwarded to the shared media connector. For video inputs, `MediaConnector.fetch_video()` copies `self.media_io_kwargs["video"]` into `video_io_kwargs`, only setting a model-derived backend when `video_backend` is absent. `VideoMediaIO.__init__()` then consumes `video_backend` from those kwargs and loads that backend from `VIDEO_LOADER_REGISTRY`.  The relevant request-side source path is:  ```python video_io_kwargs = dict(self.media_io_kwargs.get("video", {})) if "video_backend" not in video_io_kwargs and (     video_backend := get_video_loader_backend_for_processor(video_processor) ):     video_io_kwargs["video_backend"] = video_backend video_io = VideoMediaIO(image_io, **video_io_kwargs) ```  ```python video_loader_backend = (     kwargs.pop("video_backend", None) or envs.VLLM_VIDEO_LOADER_BACKEND ) self.video_loader = VIDEO_LOADER_REGISTRY.load(video_loader_backend) ```  `VideoBackend.load_bytes()` then dispatches `backend == "pynvvideocodec"` into `decode_frames_pynvvideocodec()`, which constructs a PyNvVideoCodec decoder, creates or uses a CUDA stream, reads stream metadata, decodes selected frames on the GPU, and copies those frames into pinned host memory. The new frontend GPU memory pool accounts only for raw decoded frame bytes when a pool exists; it does not make request-time backend selection safe when no startup reservation was made.  The engine-side reservation code makes its decision from static model config and environment only:  ```python def _uses_pynvvideocodec_video_backend(mm_config) -> bool:     video_kwargs = mm_config.media_io_kwargs.get("video", {})     video_loader_backend = (         video_kwargs.get("video_backend") or envs.VLLM_VIDEO_LOADER_BACKEND     )     codec_backend = video_kwargs.get("backend")     return (         video_loader_backend == PYNVVIDEOCODEC_VIDEO_BACKEND         or codec_backend == PYNVVIDEOCODEC_VIDEO_BACKEND     ) ```  ```python decoder_reserved_bytes = (     num_api_servers * per_server_decoder_bytes     if self._uses_pynvvideocodec_video_backend(mm_config)     else 0 ) reserved_bytes = raw_frame_reserved_bytes + decoder_reserved_bytes if reserved_bytes <= 0:     return available_kv_cache_memory_bytes ```  With default static video configuration, `mm_config.media_io_kwargs["video"]` does not name PyNvVideoCodec and `VLLM_VIDEO_LOADER_BACKEND` defaults to OpenCV/software decoding. The worker therefore reserves no PyNv decoder/CUDA-context bytes. A later request can still set `media_io_kwargs.video.video_backend="pynvvideocodec"` and reach the GPU decoder path because that runtime field is intentionally honored by `VideoMediaIO`.  ## PoV  An ordinary multimodal inference request can carry the backend override in the request body:  ```json {   "model": "served-vlm",   "messages": [     {       "role": "user",       "content": [         {"type": "text", "text": "summarize this clip"},         {"type": "video_url", "video_url": {"url": "data:video/mp4;base64,<small-mp4>"}}       ]     }   ],   "media_io_kwargs": {     "video": {       "video_backend": "pynvvideocodec"     }   } } ```  The following bounded source-level check confirms the code path without allocating GPU memory:  ```bash git clone --filter=blob:none https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm.git cd vllm git checkout ddd3855a28a561a5bb54d380c6e6b8b1e883cc4a python3 check_pynv_backend_reservation.py --repo . ```  ## PoC  The bounded check validates current source markers, simulates the exact static reservation predicate, and compares vulnerable and negative-control configurations. Key output:  ```json {   "vulnerable": true,   "head": "ddd3855a28a561a5bb54d380c6e6b8b1e883cc4a",   "reservation_simulation": {     "env_video_loader_backend": "opencv",     "request_selects_pynv_after_startup": true,     "vulnerable_static_reserved_bytes": 0,     "negative_control_static_pynv_reserved_bytes": 2066953011,     "raw_frame_only_control_reserved_bytes": 268435456,     "unreserved_decoder_bytes_when_only_request_selects_pynv": 2066953011   } } ```  The negative control is important: when PyNvVideoCodec is selected statically, the worker reserves `2066953011` bytes per API process for decoder surfaces plus CUDA context. The vulnerable case reserves `0` bytes for the same decoder overhead because PyNvVideoCodec is selected only by the later request. A second control with static OpenCV plus `mm_ipc_gpu_memory_gb=0.25` reserves only the raw-frame semaphore budget and still does not reserve PyNv decoder/CUDA-context bytes.  ## Impact  An attacker who can submit video requests to a vLLM deployment with PyNvVideoCodec available can force frontend GPU decoding even when the engine did not reserve memory for that decoder during startup. On high-utilization serving deployments, the unreserved CUDA context, retained decoder surfaces, and decoded-frame allocations can reduce or exhaust GPU memory that the engine assumed was available for weights, activations, or KV cache, causing request failures, worker crashes, or service-level denial of service.  Suggested severity is Medium with conservative CVSS v3.1 `CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:L/UI:N/S:U/C:N/I:N/A:H` (6.5). If a deployment exposes the affected API without authentication, `PR:N` would raise the deployment-specific score. Suggested weaknesses are `CWE-770` (Allocation of Resources Without Limits or Throttling) and `CWE-400` (Uncontrolled Resource Consumption). This should not be rated Low because the affected resource is shared GPU memory in the serving path and the code already treats the PyNv decoder/CUDA-context footprint as large enough to reserve at startup when statically configured.  Limitations: exploitation requires a GPU deployment where PyNvVideoCodec is installed and usable, and the request must reach a video-capable model/path. The issue does not claim code execution, data disclosure, or SSRF.  ## Suggested Fix  Do not allow untrusted request fields to select a GPU decoder that was not included in startup memory reservation. The simplest fix is to reject request-level `media_io_kwargs.video.video_backend="pynvvideocodec"` unless the static server configuration already selected PyNvVideoCodec and reserved its decoder/CUDA-context budget.  If dynamic backend selection remains supported, split software and GPU decoder policies: allow request selection among CPU/software decoders only, require an explicit operator allowlist for GPU decoders, and include every request-selectable GPU decoder in the startup reservation predicate. Add regression coverage for static OpenCV startup config plus request-level PyNvVideoCodec override, and preserve the negative control where static PyNvVideoCodec configuration reserves decoder/CUDA-context bytes.  ## Affected Package/Versions  Package: `vllm` from `vllm-project/vllm`. vLLM through 0.29.0 fetches and fully materializes remote or inline media before enforcing its documented media controls (the VLLM_MAX_AUDIO_CLIP_FILESIZE_MB compressed-audio size cap, default 25 MB, and the per-modality --limit-mm-per-prompt item limits). Across four ingress paths — the shared media-acquisition layer (HTTPConnection.get_bytes()/async_get_bytes()), the chat completions audio_url/base64 path, the batch speech runner, and the Rust frontend POST /tokenize route — the server reads the entire HTTP response body, base64-decodes the inline payload, or spawns one fetch/decode task per media part, and only then applies the limit (or, on some paths, never applies it). A remote attacker can therefore cause the API server or batch-runner process to allocate memory and consume outbound bandwidth proportional to an attacker-chosen body size or media item count before the request is rejected, resulting in pre-inference memory and bandwidth exhaustion (denial of service). The chat and batch surfaces require an API key when one is configured; the Rust frontend /tokenize route is unauthenticated by design. There is no code execution or data disclosure impact.

vLLM is an inference and serving engine for large language models. Prior to 0.28.0, the default mirrored multimodal LRU cache can commit a media hash in the frontend sender cache during multimodal rendering and before engine admission, while the engine receiver cache never receives the payload if that request is rejected. A later request reusing the same media hash causes MultiModalProcessorSenderCache to send no payload and MultiModalReceiverCache to reach an assertion with the message "Expected a cached item," producing a shared-service availability failure. ## Affected  - **Ecosystem / package:** pip / `vllm` - **Affected versions:** vLLM ≤ 0.25.1 (confirmed on 0.25.1, commit [`752a3a504485`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/tree/752a3a504485790a2e8491cacbb35c137339ad34)). The lower bound predates 0.25.1; maintainers can confirm how far back the tool-continuation re-submission has omitted the salt.  ## Summary  On the GPT-OSS "Harmony" path (`POST /v1/responses`), a request that uses a built-in or MCP tool runs as a multi-turn loop: after each tool call vLLM re-renders the full next-turn Harmony prompt and re-submits it to the engine. Turn 1 correctly carries `request.cache_salt`, but the tool-continuation re-submission rebuilds the engine input via `tokens_input(token_ids)` with **no** `cache_salt`. The continuation prefix is therefore cached in the global *unsalted* namespace even though the caller opted into salting. A second tenant who can guess the low-entropy post-tool history submits the reconstructed continuation (unsalted) and reads exact per-turn cached-token counts from the Responses usage — restoring the prompt-membership oracle that `cache_salt` is documented to prevent.  Silently dropping a preserved salt *after* the supported tool workflow is enabled is a broken isolation control: the caller enabled salting and every turn should stay isolated, but continuation turns leak into the shared cache.  This is distinct from [GHSA-4qjh-9fv9-r85r](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/security/advisories/GHSA-4qjh-9fv9-r85r) ([CVE-2025-46570](https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2025-46570)): that advisory is the prefix-cache membership oracle for which `cache_salt` is the documented mitigation, and its PR-17045 fix does not close this site — the Harmony tool continuation silently drops the preserved salt, caching in the unsalted namespace and leaking exact `cached_tokens_per_turn` counts from a different sink (the Responses serving continuation, not general TTFT timing).  ## Affected code  Links pinned to the confirmed commit [`752a3a504485`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/tree/752a3a504485790a2e8491cacbb35c137339ad34) (v0.25.1):  - **The drop (sink):** [`vllm/entrypoints/openai/responses/serving.py#L712-L713`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/752a3a504485790a2e8491cacbb35c137339ad34/vllm/entrypoints/openai/responses/serving.py#L712-L713) — `token_ids = context.render_for_completion()` then `engine_input = tokens_input(token_ids)`, with no `cache_salt`. - **Correct turn-1 call for contrast:** [`vllm/entrypoints/openai/responses/serving.py#L755`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/752a3a504485790a2e8491cacbb35c137339ad34/vllm/entrypoints/openai/responses/serving.py#L755) — `tokens_input(prompt_token_ids, cache_salt=request.cache_salt)`. - **`tokens_input` stores the salt only if passed:** [`vllm/inputs/engine.py#L51-L66`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/752a3a504485790a2e8491cacbb35c137339ad34/vllm/inputs/engine.py#L51-L66) (`if cache_salt is not None: inputs["cache_salt"] = cache_salt`). - **The engine request copies only the current input's salt:** [`vllm/v1/engine/input_processor.py#L380`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/752a3a504485790a2e8491cacbb35c137339ad34/vllm/v1/engine/input_processor.py#L380) (`cache_salt=decoder_inputs.get("cache_salt")` → `None` for the continuation). - **Prefix-cache hashing keys on the salt only when present:** [`vllm/v1/core/kv_cache_utils.py#L560-L561`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/752a3a504485790a2e8491cacbb35c137339ad34/vllm/v1/core/kv_cache_utils.py#L560-L561) (`[request.cache_salt] if (start_token_idx == 0 and request.cache_salt) else []`). - **The oracle the attacker reads:** [`vllm/entrypoints/openai/responses/serving.py#L909`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/752a3a504485790a2e8491cacbb35c137339ad34/vllm/entrypoints/openai/responses/serving.py#L909) (`cached_tokens_per_turn`). - **The documented control being defeated:** [`vllm/entrypoints/openai/responses/protocol.py#L235`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/752a3a504485790a2e8491cacbb35c137339ad34/vllm/entrypoints/openai/responses/protocol.py#L235) (`cache_salt` field).  The tool-continuation re-submission rebuilds the engine input with no `cache_salt`:  ```python # vllm/entrypoints/openai/responses/serving.py Lines 711-715             if isinstance(context, HarmonyContext):                 token_ids = context.render_for_completion()                 engine_input = tokens_input(token_ids)                  sampling_params.max_tokens = max_model_len - len(token_ids) ```  Contrast with the correct turn-1 call, which does preserve the caller's salt:  ```python # vllm/entrypoints/openai/responses/serving.py Lines 754-755         prompt_token_ids = render_for_completion(messages)         engine_input = tokens_input(prompt_token_ids, cache_salt=request.cache_salt) ```  `tokens_input` stores the salt on the engine input only when it is passed, so the continuation input carries none and lands in the unsalted namespace:  ```python # vllm/inputs/engine.py Lines 51-66 def tokens_input(     prompt_token_ids: list[int],     *,     prompt: str | None = None,     cache_salt: str | None = None, ) -> TokensInput:     """     Construct [`TokensInput`][vllm.inputs.engine.TokensInput]     from optional values.     """     inputs = TokensInput(type="token", prompt_token_ids=prompt_token_ids)      if prompt is not None:         inputs["prompt"] = prompt     if cache_salt is not None:         inputs["cache_salt"] = cache_salt ```  ## Impact  An authenticated tenant of a shared deployment can recover whether a guessed post-tool prompt or history was processed by another tenant, with exact cached-token counts rather than noisy latency — the exact prompt-membership oracle `cache_salt` is documented to prevent. It defeats the multi-user prefix-cache isolation guarantee for salted Harmony tool sessions.  Preconditions: a GPT-OSS Harmony model on `/v1/responses`; prefix caching enabled (default); an operator-enabled built-in or MCP tool server; the victim sets `cache_salt` and triggers at least one tool continuation; and the attacker can reconstruct the post-tool history closely enough to match the token prefix. The `AC:H` metric reflects that guessable-history precondition.   ## Suggested Fix  Propagate `request.cache_salt` into every Harmony (and Parsable) tool-continuation re-submission — at the continuation call site call `tokens_input(token_ids, cache_salt=request.cache_salt)`, mirroring the correct turn-1 call. Carry the salt on the `HarmonyContext` (thread the originating `request` into the context) so no continuation path can omit it:  ```diff # vllm/entrypoints/openai/responses/serving.py              if isinstance(context, HarmonyContext):                  token_ids = context.render_for_completion() -                engine_input = tokens_input(token_ids) +                engine_input = tokens_input( +                    token_ids, +                    cache_salt=( +                        context.request.cache_salt +                        if context.request is not None +                        else None +                    ), +                ) ```  with `HarmonyContext.__init__` gaining a `request: ResponsesRequest | None = None` parameter (stored as `self.request`) that `_create_responses` passes when constructing the context. The continuation prefix is then cached in the victim's salted namespace, mirroring turn 1.  Suggested regression test: assert `cached_tokens_per_turn == 0` for a different-salt probe against a salted victim continuation (the four-way control from the proof of concept).  ## Credit  **Reported by:** Patch the Planet (Trail of Bits + OpenAI collaboration)  This vulnerability was discovered using GPT-5.5-Cyber as part of the Patch the Planet security initiative.  ---  **Proposed fix:** a fix for this issue is proposed in a public pull request: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/51818

vLLM is an inference and serving engine for large language models. Prior to 0.30.0, the Rust frontend's track_http_metrics middleware records the raw HTTP method token as a Prometheus label for requests reaching registered routes. An unauthenticated attacker can send unique arbitrary method tokens to unguarded routes such as /tokenize, causing Prometheus's Family::get_or_create function to permanently create counter and histogram label sets. Those label sets increase process memory usage and enlarge the /metrics response until the service or monitoring path is exhausted. This issue is fixed in version 0.30.0.

vLLM is an inference and serving engine for large language models. Prior to 0.32.0, an authenticated caller can place forged shared-memory address and monotonic_id values in public multimodal features.kwargs_data. In scale-out deployments with shared-memory multimodal caching enabled, workers trust those values and pass attacker-selected bytes to pickle.loads(), allowing arbitrary Python execution even when insecure serialization is disabled. This issue is fixed in version 0.32.0.

vLLM is an inference and serving engine for large language models. Prior to 0.32.0, the OpenAI-compatible server configures Starlette CORSMiddleware with allowed_origins set to a wildcard by default. A malicious web page can use a victim's browser to reach an unauthenticated vLLM server on localhost, an internal network, or a VPN, call endpoints including GET /v1/models and POST /v1/chat/completions, consume GPU resources, and read responses. Cookie-based cross-site request forgery does not apply because credentials are disabled by default, and deployments requiring bearer authentication are exposed only when the caller already has a usable token. This issue is fixed in version 0.32.0.

vLLM is an inference and serving engine for large language models. Prior to 0.32.0, vllm/tokenizers/hf.py computes max_token_id with an off-by-one upper bound, allowing a pre-tokenized prompt ID equal to the vocabulary size to pass validation. For a tensor-parallel size of one and an exact multiple-of-64 vocabulary, VocabParallelEmbedding.forward does not mask that value before F.embedding uses it, causing a CUDA device-side assertion and terminating the engine. This issue is fixed in version 0.32.0.

### Summary A recent review identified several regular expressions in the vllm codebase that are susceptible to Regular Expression Denial of Service (ReDoS) attacks. These patterns, if fed with crafted or malicious input, may cause severe performance degradation due to catastrophic backtracking.  #### 1. vllm/lora/utils.py [Line 173](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/2858830c39da0ae153bc1328dbba7680f5fbebe1/vllm/lora/utils.py#L173)  https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/2858830c39da0ae153bc1328dbba7680f5fbebe1/vllm/lora/utils.py#L173 **Risk Description:** - The regex `r"\((.*?)\)\$?$"` matches content inside parentheses. If input such as `((((a|)+)+)+)` is passed in, it can cause catastrophic backtracking, leading to a ReDoS vulnerability. - Using `.*?` (non-greedy match) inside group parentheses can be highly sensitive to input length and nesting complexity.  **Remediation Suggestions:** - Limit the input string length. - Use a non-recursive matching approach, or write a regex with stricter content constraints. - Consider using possessive quantifiers or atomic groups (not supported in Python yet), or split and process before regex matching.  ---  #### 2. vllm/entrypoints/openai/tool_parsers/phi4mini_tool_parser.py [Line 52](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/2858830c39da0ae153bc1328dbba7680f5fbebe1/vllm/entrypoints/openai/tool_parsers/phi4mini_tool_parser.py#L52)  https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/2858830c39da0ae153bc1328dbba7680f5fbebe1/vllm/entrypoints/openai/tool_parsers/phi4mini_tool_parser.py#L52  **Risk Description:** - The regex `r'functools\[(.*?)\]'` uses `.*?` to match content inside brackets, together with `re.DOTALL`. If the input contains a large number of nested or crafted brackets, it can cause backtracking and ReDoS.  **Remediation Suggestions:** - Limit the length of `model_output`. - Use a stricter, non-greedy pattern (avoid matching across extraneous nesting). - Prefer `re.finditer()` and enforce a length constraint on each match.  ---  #### 3. vllm/entrypoints/openai/serving_chat.py [Line 351](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/2858830c39da0ae153bc1328dbba7680f5fbebe1/vllm/entrypoints/openai/serving_chat.py#L351)  https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/2858830c39da0ae153bc1328dbba7680f5fbebe1/vllm/entrypoints/openai/serving_chat.py#L351  **Risk Description:** - The regex `r'.*"parameters":\s*(.*)'` can trigger backtracking if `current_text` is very long and contains repeated structures. - Especially when processing strings from unknown sources, `.*` matching any content is high risk.  **Remediation Suggestions:** - Use a more specific pattern (e.g., via JSON parsing). - Impose limits on `current_text` length. - Avoid using `.*` to capture large blocks of text; prefer structured parsing when possible.  ---  #### 4. benchmarks/benchmark_serving_structured_output.py [Line 650](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/2858830c39da0ae153bc1328dbba7680f5fbebe1/benchmarks/benchmark_serving_structured_output.py#L650)  https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/2858830c39da0ae153bc1328dbba7680f5fbebe1/benchmarks/benchmark_serving_structured_output.py#L650  **Risk Description:** - The regex `r'\{.*\}'` is used to extract JSON inside curly braces. If the `actual` string is very long with unbalanced braces, it can cause backtracking, leading to a ReDoS vulnerability. - Although this is used for benchmark correctness checking, it should still handle abnormal inputs carefully.  **Remediation Suggestions:** - Limit the length of `actual`. - Prefer stepwise search for `{` and `}` or use a robust JSON extraction tool. - Recommend first locating the range with simple string search, then applying regex.  ### Fix  * https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/18454  ---

## Summary  Multimodal content parts (`image_url`, `video_url`, `input_audio`, ...) accept a user-supplied `uuid` field that vLLM uses **verbatim as the item's cache identity** (`mm_hash`). The two frontend/engine processor caches (P0 "sender" cache in the API process, P1 "receiver" cache in the EngineCore process) are independent LRU caches whose evictions are **not synchronized**, and the P1 hit path performs **zero consistency validation** — it silently substitutes the cached item's tensor data for whatever the current request actually contains.  A single unauthenticated client can exploit this to kill the entire engine, deterministically, with default server flags:  1. **Seed**: send a small image with `uuid="U"`. Both caches now map `U` to an item with **N_A** visual tokens (e.g. 4). 2. **Drift**: send ~70 requests, each carrying a *unique* uuid, a max-size image, and an over-long text prompt. Each request is rejected with 400 — but **after** its image has been inserted into the P0 cache (insertion happens during chat rendering, before prompt-length validation), so these requests fill P0 **without ever reaching the engine/P1**. `U` is evicted from P0 only. 3. **Kill**: send a *large* image with `uuid="U"`. P0 misses → the image is freshly processed and the prompt is spliced with **N_B** (e.g. 2048+) placeholder tokens; the request carries full data to the engine, but P1 still has `U` → the engine **discards the fresh data and substitutes the stale N_A-row tensor**. The scheduler plans for N_B encoder slots while the worker merges N_A embeddings into N_B placeholders → `ValueError: Attempted to assign 4 = 4 multimodal tokens to 2048 placeholders` at `vllm/model_executor/models/utils.py:711` → uncaught in the EngineCore busy loop → `_send_engine_dead()` → the EngineCore process dies, every API server reports `EngineDeadError` and shuts down. `/health` never recovers; the deployment needs a full restart.  Verified end-to-end on the official `vllm/vllm-openai:v0.29.0` image with Qwen2.5-VL-3B-Instruct, default configuration (no flags beyond `--served-model-name`/`--gpu-memory-utilization`): after 70 flood requests the kill request returned `500 EngineCore encountered an issue` and `/health` went dead permanently. The vulnerable code is byte-identical on `main` (post-0.29.0).  ## Details  **1. The client-controlled `uuid` becomes the cache hash verbatim.** `vllm/entrypoints/chat_utils.py:1677` / `:1884-1886` read `part["uuid"]` per content part and pass it through as `mm_uuids`. In `vllm/multimodal/processing/inputs.py:62-63`, when no `hf_processor_mm_kwargs` are present (the default for chat requests), the uuid string **is** the item hash — no content binding at all:  ```python # vllm/multimodal/processing/inputs.py:62-63 else:     hashes.append(uuid_item)        # client string used verbatim as mm_hash ```  **2. P0 insertion happens before request validation.** In the serving path, `render_chat_request` (`vllm/entrypoints/openai/chat_completion/serving.py:275`) runs full mm processing — `mm_processor.apply` (`vllm/renderers/base.py:759`) → `_cached_apply_hf_processor` → `_merge_mm_kwargs` → `cache.get_and_update_item` (`vllm/multimodal/processing/processor.py:1338`), which inserts the processed item into the P0 sender cache (default `mm_processor_cache_type="lru"`, 4 GiB). Only afterwards does `get_max_tokens` (`vllm/entrypoints/serve/utils/api_utils.py:183-186`) reject over-long prompts with 400. **A request can therefore write to P0 while never reaching the engine** — the primitive that desynchronizes P0 from P1. (Public issue #43941 documented this same asymmetry for the opposite drift direction, which was later handled via `MultiModalCacheMissError`; the P0-miss/P1-hit direction below was never addressed.)  **3. P1 substitutes cached data on hash hit with no consistency check.** In the EngineCore input thread, `preprocess_add_request` (`vllm/v1/engine/core.py:997-1000`) calls `mm_receiver_cache.get_and_update_features`, which only replaces `feature.data` (`vllm/multimodal/cache.py:673-690`) and keeps the request's own `mm_position` (placeholder layout). On a cache hit the receiver cache returns the stale item wholesale:  ```python # vllm/multimodal/cache.py:739-740  (MultiModalReceiverCache.get_and_update_item) if (cached_item := self._cache.get(mm_hash)) is not None:     return cached_item              # fresh data silently discarded; no size/modality check ```  Only the opposite drift (P0 hit / P1 miss, `data=None`) is handled, via the retryable `MultiModalCacheMissError`. Nothing validates that the cached item's modality, shape, or token count matches the current request's placeholders.  **4. The mismatch is fatal to the engine.** The scheduler plans encoder work from the request's (fresh) placeholder count N_B, while the worker gathers embeddings from the stale N_A-row tensor (encoder-cache hit under the same forged hash, or re-encoding the stale data — both yield N_A rows). `_merge_multimodal_embeddings` then raises:  ```python # vllm/model_executor/models/utils.py:703-714 inputs_embeds[is_multimodal] = mm_embeds_flat.to(dtype=input_dtype)   # RuntimeError ... raise ValueError(     f"Attempted to assign {expr} = {num_actual_tokens} "     f"multimodal tokens to {num_expected_tokens} placeholders") from e ```  This exception is raised inside the worker's input preparation with no per-request containment, propagates to the EngineCore busy loop's top-level handler (`vllm/v1/engine/core.py:1372`), and triggers `_send_engine_dead()`. The API server's `output_handler` receives `EngineDeadError` (`vllm/v1/engine/async_llm.py:819`) and the whole process tree shuts down. (Issue #55546 independently reported this sink — "one bad multimodal item kills the entire V1 engine tree" — from an organically occurring stale cache entry; this report provides the missing deterministic, remote, single-attacker trigger.)  **Cost of the attack.** With the default `mm_processor_cache_gb=4`, one max-size Qwen2.5-VL image (12845056 pixels) caches as ~77 MB, so ~56 flood requests suffice; we used 70. Flood requests are CPU-only image decodes (~0.3 s each here) and can be issued sequentially or concurrently; the total wall-clock cost of the kill was under one minute. Models with larger `max_pixels` fill the cache in even fewer requests. Note that issuing the flood with *successful* requests does not work — they would populate P1 as well; rejection after P0 insertion is essential, and the over-long-prompt 400 is one always-available way to get it (no size limits depend on non-default flags).   ## Impact  Any unauthenticated client that can reach a multimodal vLLM endpoint (`/v1/chat/completions`, `/v1/responses`, etc. — all accept content-part `uuid`) can **deterministically crash the entire serving instance**: the EngineCore process dies, every in-flight request fails, and the API server exits; the deployment stays down until restarted. In data-parallel or multi-API-server deployments the blast radius extends to the whole engine group (cf. the DP8 outage in #55546). The attack requires no special privileges, no non-default server flags, no race conditions, and costs under a minute of sequential requests at default cache sizes.  This is distinct from the documented "Multimodal Media UUID Security" guidance in `docs/usage/security.md`, which covers only **integrity/confidentiality** consequences of uuid collisions (a caller silently receiving another caller's media). The guidance does not mention availability, and following it does not help: the attacker here deliberately collides with *their own* uuid, and the fatal element is the missing consistency check on the P1 hit path plus the unsynchronized eviction of the two caches.  **Suggested remediation** (any one of these breaks the kill chain):  1. On a P1 receiver-cache hit, validate the cached item against the request's `mm_position` (modality and expected embedding count); on mismatch, treat it as a miss (`MultiModalCacheMissError`) or reject the request — never substitute silently. 2. Make the feature/placeholder count mismatch in `_merge_multimodal_embeddings` a per-request error instead of a fatal engine exception (also requested by #55546). 3. Bind server-side cache identity to content even when a uuid is provided (e.g. `hash(content) + uuid`), eliminating forged-hash cache hits entirely. 4. Synchronize P0/P1 evictions (the engine already pushes `invalidate` to P0 on cache-miss; eviction-direction sync would close the remaining drift).  A public fix is available here: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/57833

## Summary  API clients can supply arbitrary `mm_processor_kwargs` per request. vLLM forwards these values through the multimodal rendering and processing pipeline to Hugging Face and custom image/video processor constructors and calls. Resource-sensitive values such as image size, patch size, patch count, crop count, or frame count can therefore be controlled by a remote client.  For processors that upscale inputs, a single request can force an allocation large enough to terminate the API server or worker with an out-of-memory condition.  ## Affected Components  The per-request field was introduced in commit `041e29471671a3d43afedb6a749421d56ef4d3e7` and first shipped in v0.7.3. The generic forwarding path remains present in current `main`.  The Isaac path is a concrete high-amplification example:  - `ChatCompletionRequest.mm_processor_kwargs` - `OnlineRenderer` request extras - `MMProcessorInputs.hf_processor_mm_kwargs` - `BaseMultiModalProcessor.info.get_hf_processor(**hf_processor_mm_kwargs)` - `IsaacProcessingInfo.get_image_processor(**kwargs)` - `IsaacImageProcessor(**kwargs)` - `process_vision_for_patches()`  Equivalent constructor forwarding exists in InternVL-derived processors, H2OVL, Step3VL, NemotronVL, and other multimodal processors. The issue is at the shared remote-input boundary and is not limited to a fixed model list.  ## Impact  - **Availability:** one request can exhaust CPU or GPU memory and terminate a   shared service process. - **Scope:** all users of the affected service instance lose availability. - **Authentication:** vLLM's API key is optional, so deployments without an   external authentication layer are remotely reachable without privileges.  ## Remediation  Reject non-empty per-request `mm_processor_kwargs` at every API-server request schema by default. Operators serving only trusted clients can explicitly opt in to the existing override behavior. Server-level `--mm-processor-kwargs` and offline `LLM` overrides remain available.  This shared boundary covers current and future multimodal processors instead of maintaining a model-specific list or a denylist that can miss custom processor arguments.  A patch for this was merged here: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/58830

## Summary  An untrusted multimodal request can set `mm_processor_kwargs.code_revision`. When vLLM serves a model whose Hugging Face processor uses dynamic `auto_map` code and the operator enabled `--trust-remote-code`, this request value reaches `AutoProcessor.from_pretrained` and selects the Python revision imported by Transformers.  This lets a client replace the operator-reviewed processor module with code from another revision of the same model repository. The operator-selected model/data `revision` remains pinned; only the executed processor code changes.  Importing a Python module is arbitrary code execution in the vLLM API/renderer process. The PoC below demonstrates this with an import-time filesystem write. It is fully offline and does not require a GPU, model weights, or changes to a real Hub repository.  ## Affected snapshot  - Repository: [`vllm-project/vllm`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm) - Verified commit: [`570735520942b6428ae98f1eb442c6d88adae55e`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/commit/570735520942b6428ae98f1eb442c6d88adae55e) - Verified with Transformers 5.15.0 and 5.16.1 - Affected release range has not been bisected  ## Affected configuration  The vulnerable path exists when all of the following are true:  1. The served model's processor uses dynamic `auto_map.AutoProcessor` code. 2. The operator enabled `trust_remote_code`. 3. The server can fetch the request-selected revision, or it is already cached. 4. The attacker can create or otherwise control a revision in the served model repository. An example is a [Hugging Face community pull-request ref](https://huggingface.co/docs/hub/en/repositories-pull-requests-discussions#where-in-the-git-repo-are-changes-stored) when that repository permits them. 5. A multimodal request reaches the processor path.  The default `trust_remote_code=False` configuration is not affected.  ## Attack surface  `mm_processor_kwargs` is accepted directly by public request models:  - [`TokenizeChatRequest.mm_processor_kwargs`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/570735520942b6428ae98f1eb442c6d88adae55e/vllm/entrypoints/serve/tokenize/protocol.py#L111-L114) - [`ChatCompletionRequest.mm_processor_kwargs`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/570735520942b6428ae98f1eb442c6d88adae55e/vllm/entrypoints/openai/chat_completion/protocol.py#L372-L375)  `/tokenize` is particularly relevant because vLLM's authentication middleware guards only `/v1`, `/v2`, `/inference`, and `/cohere` prefixes:  - [`AuthenticationMiddleware`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/570735520942b6428ae98f1eb442c6d88adae55e/vllm/entrypoints/serve/middleware/authenticate.py#L11-L62)  Consequently, `/tokenize` remains unauthenticated even when `--api-key` is configured, unless an external proxy protects it. The vLLM [Security Guide](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/usage/security/#unprotected-endpoints-no-api-key-required) documents `/tokenize` as an unprotected endpoint.  ## Root cause  The request value follows this path:  1. [`OnlineRenderer.preprocess_chat`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/570735520942b6428ae98f1eb442c6d88adae55e/vllm/renderers/online_renderer.py#L406-L435) places request `mm_processor_kwargs` in prompt extras. 2. Multimodal rendering forwards those kwargs into processor construction through [`MMProcessorInputs`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/570735520942b6428ae98f1eb442c6d88adae55e/vllm/renderers/base.py#L751-L760) and [`_process_multimodal_async`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/570735520942b6428ae98f1eb442c6d88adae55e/vllm/renderers/base.py#L831-L847). 3. [`MultiModalConfig.merge_mm_processor_kwargs`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/570735520942b6428ae98f1eb442c6d88adae55e/vllm/config/multimodal.py#L506-L518) overlays inference values on startup values, so the request wins. 4. [`cached_get_processor_without_dynamic_kwargs`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/570735520942b6428ae98f1eb442c6d88adae55e/vllm/transformers_utils/processor.py#L344-L375) filters only recognized processor-call keys. `code_revision` is retained as a processor-construction kwarg. 5. [`cached_processor_from_config`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/570735520942b6428ae98f1eb442c6d88adae55e/vllm/transformers_utils/processor.py#L380-L390) pins `revision` and `trust_remote_code`, but forwards the remaining kwargs without reserving `code_revision`. 6. [`get_processor`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/570735520942b6428ae98f1eb442c6d88adae55e/vllm/transformers_utils/processor.py#L205-L245) calls `AutoProcessor.from_pretrained(..., revision=revision, trust_remote_code=trust_remote_code, **kwargs)`. 7. Transformers [`AutoProcessor.from_pretrained`](https://github.com/huggingface/transformers/blob/v5.15.0/src/transformers/models/auto/processing_auto.py#L294-L302) uses `code_revision` to retrieve and import the dynamic module through [`get_class_from_dynamic_module`](https://github.com/huggingface/transformers/blob/v5.15.0/src/transformers/dynamic_module_utils.py#L474-L575), then removes it before loading processor data. This is why code comes from the attacker revision while configuration/data remain operator-pinned.  Request-time processor arguments are not separated from processor-construction arguments, and `code_revision` is not reserved.  ## Suggested remediation  1. Separate processor-construction arguments from untrusted processor-call arguments. An allowlist of supported request-time preprocessing controls is safest. 2. Reject `code_revision` and other loader/source controls in request `mm_processor_kwargs`, and pass `model_config.code_revision` explicitly as the only permitted processor-code revision. 3. Add a regression test proving a request cannot change the loaded module revision while operator pins remain effective. 4. Protect `/tokenize` with the configured authentication policy as defense in depth.  Expected safe behavior is either a 4xx response for reserved request keys or silently ignoring them before processor construction. Rejection is preferable because it makes attempted misuse visible.  A patch for this was merged here: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/58830

### Summary  The Phi-4 multimodal audio encoder (`phi4mm_audio.py` / `phi4mm_utils.py`) runs its conformer attention in **eager mode by default**: the official HF config of `microsoft/Phi-4-multimodal-instruct` does not set `use_pt_scaled_dot_product_attention`, so the default `False` applies (`phi4mm_audio.py:166`, `:876`; `phi4mm_utils.py:1669`). The eager path fully materializes the attention probability matrix of shape `[n_chunks, 16, 500, 500]` per layer — and then **stores it on the module**: `self.attn = attn` (`phi4mm_utils.py:1802`, a `torch.jit.Attribute` declared at `:1693`), keeping a live reference for every one of the 24 encoder layers.  The only gates on audio length are the server-side limits `VLLM_MAX_AUDIO_CLIP_FILESIZE_MB=25` and `VLLM_MAX_AUDIO_DECODE_DURATION_S=600` (`envs.py:83-84`) — i.e. a 10-minute clip is a **legal input by default**. A 600 s clip becomes ~60,000 mel frames, which the encoder unfolds into 500-frame chunks (`phi4mm_audio.py:996`, `max_seq_len = 500`), giving `n_chunks ≈ 120`. Each layer therefore materializes a `120×16×500×500` matrix (~1–2 GiB depending on dtype), and the module attribute keeps all completed layers' matrices alive, so GPU memory climbs monotonically **within a single request** until an allocation fails.  Verified end-to-end on the official `vllm/vllm-openai:v0.31.0` image: one 19.2 MB silent 600 s WAV → worker `torch.OutOfMemoryError: CUDA out of memory. Tried to allocate 2.29 GiB ... 501.75 MiB free ... 22.09 GiB allocated by PyTorch` inside `get_audio_features` (`phi4mm_audio.py:1279` → `:1332` → `phi4mm_utils.py:1386`) → `EngineCore encountered a fatal error` → API `EngineDeadError` → whole server down; `/health` refuses connections. Total time from request to dead service: **~6 seconds**.  A secondary effect: because `self.attn` persists on the module after the request ends, the matrices of the last audio request stay resident indefinitely (observed +50 MiB pinned after a single 5 s control request); they are only overwritten by the next audio request, so the resident footprint equals the largest audio processed since startup.  ### Details  **1. Root cause.** `MultiHeadedAttention.forward_attention` in eager mode computes `attn = masked_softmax(scores, mask)` and unconditionally executes `self.attn = attn` (`phi4mm_utils.py:1795-1802`). The attribute is a leftover inference/debug hook (used by `torch.jit.Attribute(None, Tensor | None)` at `:1693`); in serving it serves no purpose but pins the full `[batch·chunks, heads, T, T]` tensor per layer past both the layer's forward and the request's lifetime. The SDP attention branch (`use_pt_scaled_dot_product_attention=True`) never materializes this matrix — but the HF config does not enable it and the code default is `False`.  **2. Why one request suffices.** The conformer chunks long audio to `max_seq_len = 500` frames (`phi4mm_audio.py:996`). Duration is bounded only by `VLLM_MAX_AUDIO_DECODE_DURATION_S=600`, so `n_chunks` reaches ~120 for a maximal clip. With 16 heads and fp32 scores, one layer's attention tensor is ~1.8 GiB (the observed failing allocation was 2.29 GiB, consistent with the scores+bias materialization). The encoder has `num_blocks=24`, `attention_heads=16`, `attention_dim=1024`, `time_reduction=8` (HF config). Weights plus a handful of retained per-layer matrices exhaust the ~2.3 GiB headroom that `--gpu-memory-utilization 0.9` leaves on a 24 GB card — mid-forward, on the first request.  **4. Deployment reality.** `--trust-remote-code` is the documented, standard way to serve this model (the HF model card instructs it), so the finding applies to default deployments. The crash is deterministic, not load-dependent: scheduler stats at death show a single running request and near-zero KV cache usage.   ### Impact  Any unauthenticated client that can reach the chat/completions API of a default deployment serving `Phi-4-multimodal-instruct` (or any model reusing this audio tower) can kill the entire engine with **one request** carrying a perfectly legal 10-minute audio clip (silent noise suffices — no crafted content needed). Full denial of service, requiring a process restart. On GPUs with more headroom (e.g. 80 GB at default utilization) a single request may survive, but the eager path still materializes GiB-scale per-layer matrices and retains the last request's tensors indefinitely, so a few sequential max-length requests — or normal traffic following one — achieve the same result.  Relation to prior art: the only public Phi-4-mm advisory we found, GHSA-vc6m-hm49-g9qg, concerns a CPU-side quadratic-cost path — different subsystem, different mechanism. GitHub search for "phi4mm audio OOM/memory" (31 results, 2026-10-08) shows no report of this attention-retention issue; `main` (2026-10-08) is unchanged.  **Suggested remediation** (any one breaks the chain; 1+2 recommended):  1. Remove `self.attn = attn` from the serving path (or gate it behind an explicit debug/`output_attentions` flag) so attention matrices are freed when the layer returns. 2. Default `use_pt_scaled_dot_product_attention` to `True` (flash/SDPA kernels never materialize the `[B, H, T, T]` matrix); keep eager only as an opt-in. 3. Additionally bound the encoder input (frames or duration) for this model so the eager path cannot reach GiB-scale single-layer allocations even if enabled.  This advisory was fixed in [MR60614](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/60614).

### Summary  In vLLM 0.30.0, `ImageMediaIO` passes attacker-controlled image bytes to Pillow's format autodetection without restricting the accepted formats; the request's MIME label does not constrain decoder selection. An EPS payload labeled `image/png` reached the host's Ghostscript executable. On a host with Ghostscript affected by CVE-2024-29510, this exposes the known Ghostscript sandbox escape through vLLM's image-loading path and can execute commands with the vLLM process's privileges. A bounded marker-command payload executed through the PyPI wheel's actual `ImageMediaIO.load_base64()` implementation using Debian Ghostscript 10.03.0. The loader-level execution is reproduced; the HTTP request path is source-traced but was not exercised end to end. This report concerns vLLM's untrusted-format dispatch and does not claim a new Ghostscript vulnerability. Exploitation requires an image-capable request path, a caller able to reach it under the deployment's authentication policy, and a vulnerable host Ghostscript build.  ### Details  `ImageMediaIO` is the boundary where attacker-controlled bytes enter Pillow's format autodetection: the declared MIME type does not constrain decoder selection, and the loader calls `Image.open(BytesIO(data))` without a Pillow format allowlist. Pillow recognizes EPS by its file signature, and vLLM's subsequent `image.load()` call enters Pillow's EPS processing path. The OpenAI chat multimodal parser reaches this path through [`parse_image()` and `fetch_image()`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/bc21cba9673cfc2256a2726b4bc32f062237cd35/vllm/entrypoints/chat_utils.py#L1077-L1081) and the [media connector](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/bc21cba9673cfc2256a2726b4bc32f062237cd35/vllm/multimodal/media/connector.py#L367-L402); the data URL path extracts the MIME label and forwards the bytes to the loader ([source](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/bc21cba9673cfc2256a2726b4bc32f062237cd35/vllm/multimodal/media/connector.py#L319-L332)). This is the vLLM-specific issue: untrusted image bytes can select a Pillow-supported format parser. Each downstream impact depends on the relevant parser, component version, and host configuration.  Pillow recognizes EPS by its file signature and invokes Ghostscript with `-dSAFER`, `-sDEVICE=pnmraw`, and the untrusted EPS input ([Pillow EPS plugin](https://github.com/python-pillow/Pillow/blob/12.3.0/src/PIL/EpsImagePlugin.py#L132-L159), [load path](https://github.com/python-pillow/Pillow/blob/12.3.0/src/PIL/EpsImagePlugin.py#L405-L415)). The command execution in this report uses the already-known Ghostscript CVE-2024-29510, which allows crafted PostScript to bypass `-dSAFER`; Ghostscript lists 10.03.1 as the upstream fixed version ([Ghostscript CVE details](https://www.ghostscript.com/releases/cve/index.html)). This is an N-day dependency chain: CVE-2024-29510 provides the command-execution primitive, while the vLLM-specific issue is that untrusted, remotely supplied image bytes can reach the affected interpreter. No new Ghostscript flaw is claimed here.  The vLLM Python requirements declare Pillow but not Ghostscript, so this execution chain depends on a Ghostscript executable supplied by the host or deployment image. I reproduced command execution with the PyPI `vllm==0.30.0` wheel, Pillow 12.3.0, and Debian amd64 Ghostscript `10.03.0~dfsg-1`. The Codean Labs CVE-2024-29510 testkit identified that Ghostscript build as vulnerable. The adapted EPS payload ran only `touch` on a temporary marker. The marker existed after the loader call, although Pillow then raised `ValueError` because the exploit changes Ghostscript's output device. The API route was traced in source but a model-backed HTTP request was not run. Only PyPI `vllm==0.30.0` was checked; no wider affected release range or other Ghostscript vendor build is claimed.  The same input boundary also exposes a separate Pillow-only denial-of-service condition when the installed Pillow version is 12.0.0–12.2.0. CVE-2026-59203 is triggered by a negative `%%BeginBinary` byte count and causes Pillow's EPS parser to loop during `Image.open()`; it does not invoke Ghostscript or provide code execution ([Pillow advisory](https://github.com/python-pillow/Pillow/security/advisories/GHSA-pg7v-jwj7-p798)). The published [`vllm==0.30.0` requirements](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/v0.30.0/requirements/common.txt#L21) leave Pillow unpinned, so an existing environment can retain an affected Pillow version; the source at commit `bc21cba9673cfc2256a2726b4bc32f062237cd35` requires [`pillow>=12.3.0`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/bc21cba9673cfc2256a2726b4bc32f062237cd35/requirements/common.txt#L22). In an isolated local check with Pillow 12.2.0, the official sample hung through `ImageMediaIO.load_bytes()` and `MediaConnector.fetch_image_async()`. Eight concurrent image loads occupied the connector's eight media-loading threads and left a benign image load queued. Pillow 12.3.0 rejected the sample promptly. This confirms a conditional media-processing DoS path, separate from the Ghostscript RCE chain; full HTTP-server availability was not measured.  ### Impact  When a vLLM image-processing endpoint accepts attacker-supplied content and the host has Ghostscript affected by CVE-2024-29510, a caller who can reach the endpoint can trigger command execution as the vLLM process user. API-key authentication and network access controls determine who can reach the request path. Deployments without Ghostscript or with a build fixed for CVE-2024-29510 are not affected by this execution chain. Separately, existing environments that run vLLM 0.30.0 with Pillow 12.0.0–12.2.0 are exposed to CVE-2026-59203 through the same image-format dispatch boundary; the demonstrated impact is exhaustion of media-loading workers, and this Pillow CVE does not cause RCE. The report asks vLLM to assess and address the unsafe dispatch of untrusted image bytes and the affected dependency combinations.  This advisory was fixed in [MR60022](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/60022).
